packet.model_contract: Sales are same-quarter prior-year net_sales*(1+sales_growth). Operating income=sales*(gross_margin-sga_ratio); pretax=operating+net_nonoperating_income; attributable net income=pretax*(1-effective_tax_rate)-noncontrolling_income; EPS=attributable NI/diluted shares. OCF=total net income*ocf_to_net_income; capex=sales*capex_ratio, positive outflow. Historical diluted shares may be approximated by NI attributable/diluted EPS; disclose rounding. Gross margin and SG&A are fractions of sales. Noncontrolling interest=total NI-NI attributable. Net nonoperating=interest_income+signed interest_expense+other_income. Cash conversion and capex require seasonality caveats; no debt/cash bridge or operational units/headcount forecast is supported.
packet.analysis_scope: Analyst-defined illustrative scenario model, not official company budget. Derive defensible base from eligible history; bear/bull are adverse/favorable profitability scenarios, not numeric ascending for every driver. Contract bounds are broad guardrails, not prescribed forecast estimates. All market-to-financial mappings are analyst judgments. Finance should map only financially material reference rows (latest history, same-quarter-prior-year baseline, and supporting trends), not repeat every row. No final-period outcomes are supplied. Missing detailed cash, debt, exposure, or portfolio breakdowns must be limitations, not invented observed facts. QA evaluates a transparent illustrative model; uncertainty alone is not an error, but unsupported claims of certainty are.

history_control_assumptions.basis: Reported growth was approximately 2% in prior-year Q4, 3% in FY2026 Q1 and 1% in Q2, with Q2 organic growth flat. Base assumes modest growth between the seasonal reference and latest reading; bear assumes contraction and bull a recovery above recent growth. These are total reported-growth assumptions, without separately adding historical FX, price or mix contributions.

Prior-year Q4 gross margin was approximately 49.11%, versus 51.37% and 51.22% in recent Q1 and Q2. Base allows partial retention of recent margins while respecting the lower Q4 seasonal reference. Bear assumes deterioration below prior-year Q4; bull assumes recent margin strength persists. Cost and mix mechanisms are illustrative judgments without supplied market evidence.

Prior-year Q4 SG&A/sales was approximately 28.26%, versus 25.21% in recent Q1 and 27.05% in Q2. Base stays close to the seasonal Q4 reference rather than extrapolating Q1's low ratio. Bear assumes expense pressure and weaker sales absorption; bull assumes improved expense efficiency. Higher ratios are adverse.

Contract-defined historical component totals were 166 in prior-year Q4, 179 in recent Q1 and 55 in Q2. Base rounds to a cautious positive contribution between the latest and seasonal references; bear allows a net expense and bull a stronger positive contribution. No interest-rate, debt-balance or exceptional-gain forecast is asserted.

Reported rates were 19.8% in prior-year Q4, 20.8% in recent Q1 and 20.1% in Q2. Base rounds near the seasonal and latest references; bear assumes a higher tax burden and bull a lower burden, near the supplied FY2025 Q3 rate of 18.6%. No specific tax benefit or jurisdictional mix change is forecast.

Total less attributable net income gives 11 in prior-year Q4, 31 in recent Q1 and 12 in Q2. Base follows the latest reading and seasonal reference. Bear assumes a larger deduction from total earnings, near Q1; bull assumes a modestly smaller deduction. Ownership and subsidiary earnings details are unavailable.

Attributable earnings divided by rounded diluted EPS imply approximately 2442.6 million shares in prior-year Q4 and 2426.4 million in latest Q2. Base assumes only a modest further decline; bear allows the denominator to remain near the prior-year level and bull assumes a larger decline. Lower shares favor EPS; none of these values establishes an observed or authorized repurchase program.

Quarterly OCF/total net income was approximately 1.375 in prior-year Q4 and 1.148 in latest Q2. Base gives greater weight to the same-quarter seasonal reference but discounts its repeatability. Bear assumes weaker cash conversion; bull assumes stronger conversion above prior-year Q4. Working-capital timing is uncertain and these ratios are not annualized.

Positive capex outflow/sales was approximately 4.77% in prior-year Q4 and 5.25% in latest Q2. Base lies between these references. Bear assumes greater spending intensity and bull lower near-term cash outflow. Capital-spending timing is seasonal; no project pipeline or deferred-investment claim is supported.

signals.mechanism: Transcribed PG01 FY2026 organic-sales guidance is 0–4%, providing an outlook envelope rather than a Q4 reported-sales forecast. PG02 reports February CPI increases of 0.3% monthly seasonally adjusted and 2.4% annually unadjusted. PG04 reports January real PCE growth of 0.1%, a USD 24.6 billion decline in current-dollar goods spending and a 4.5% saving rate. Analyst interpretation: affordability pressure and modest real spending support downside volume uncertainty, while positive real PCE and the guidance range do not establish contraction. Keep the 1.5% reported-growth base; optionally apply one combined adverse sensitivity of 0–0.5 percentage points relative to the frozen control. This range is uncalibrated, and CPI is not P&G realized pricing.
signals.double_count_risk: PG02 and PG04 describe overlapping household-demand channels; use one demand stress budget. Latest history already includes negative volume and flat organic growth. Do not add historical price or FX contributions again, or impose annual organic guidance directly on quarterly reported growth.

signals.mechanism: PG01 quotes commodity-cost neutrality; its factual transcription additionally reports a USD 400 million annual after-tax tariff headwind and USD 200 million annual after-tax FX tailwind. PG03 reports first-published February final-demand PPI increases of 0.7% monthly seasonally adjusted and 3.4% annually unadjusted. Analyst interpretation: tariff and upstream inflation uncertainty can pressure costs, while company commodity neutrality and FX guidance temper a uniformly adverse interpretation. Preserve the 50% base. A single combined adverse margin sensitivity of 0–50 basis points relative to the control is illustrative; PG03's suggested 0–30 basis points belongs within that budget. Neither annual after-tax amount is a measured quarterly gross-margin effect.
signals.double_count_risk: Company guidance already incorporates commodity, tariff and FX considerations. Do not stack full PPI stress onto full guidance stress, allocate annual amounts mechanically to Q4, or repeat cost effects already embedded in historical margins. FX may affect multiple financial lines; no supplied allocation supports separate additive benefits.

signals.mechanism: The supplied quotation supports a 3.50–3.75% federal funds target range; the factual transcription states it was maintained on March 18, 2026. Analyst interpretation: this supplies a financing backdrop, but no incremental company earnings change is established without repricing, refinancing or cash-balance evidence. Preserve the USD 100 million base and existing scenarios. A hypothetical 25-basis-point sensitivity cannot be monetized without an exposed balance. Equity discount-rate effects are outside this operating forecast.
signals.double_count_risk: Historical interest income and expense are already represented in the control. Do not apply the policy rate to all debt or add an unsupported interest/tax headwind attributed to PG01.

findings.subject: Unresolved historical reconciliation contradictions
findings.finding: Original supplied excerpts confirm unresolved USD million inconsistencies: FY2025 Q3 sales less costs equals 10,082 versus gross profit 10,081; gross profit less SG&A equals 4,557 versus operating income 4,558; operating income plus component nonoperating income equals 4,662 versus pretax 4,661. FY2026 Q1 component nonoperating income equals 179, whereas pretax less operating income equals 178. Prior outputs disclose these discrepancies, but disclosure does not resolve them. Under the requested rule blocking unresolved contradictions, the supplied material cannot receive a pass.

findings.subject: Transcription-dependent source support
findings.finding: PG01's quotation supports commodity neutrality, but its 0–4% organic guidance, USD 400 million tariff headwind and USD 200 million FX tailwind depend on factual transcriptions. PG02–PG04 numerical quotation fragments agree with the extracts, while full labels, dates and adjustment bases require the located record. PG05 quotes the rate range but not the maintained decision or date. These support narrowly scoped evidence-to-assumption checks, not independent source certification.

findings.subject: Other-income classification
findings.finding: Original excerpts label other income as operating in FY2025 Q3 and FY2026 Q1/Q2, versus non-operating in FY2025 Q4. Contract aggregation is explicit and Q2 reconciles numerically, but the inconsistent original labels prevent certification of the accounting classification.

findings.subject: Dates, units and finance mappings
findings.finding: All supplied publication dates precede the cutoff. FY2025 Q4 sales of USD 20,889 million correctly anchor April–June 2026; annual columns are excluded. Reviewed ratios, signed interest aggregation, noncontrolling deductions and approximate share denominators agree with supplied history, apart from the flagged reconciliations. Percent-to-decimal conversions and positive capex treatment are consistent. Share estimates disclose rounded-EPS dependence.

findings.subject: Scenario coherence and double counting
findings.finding: All nine scenario drivers remain within contractual bounds. Every base and all unrelated bear/bull drivers match the frozen control. Only bear sales growth decreases by 0.005 and bear gross margin by 0.005. Demand signals share one stress budget; tariff/PPI signals share another. These magnitudes are explicitly uncalibrated sensitivities, not source-derived precision. Annual organic guidance is not imposed on quarterly reported growth, and annual after-tax costs are not mechanically allocated to quarterly pretax margins.

findings.subject: Unsupported rate-guidance overlap claim
findings.finding: PG05's assertion that PG01 includes annual interest/tax headwinds has no support in either supplied PG01 evidence surface. Finance, research and scenario explicitly exclude it, so it creates no modeled charge. Policy rates are appropriately kept separate from company borrowing costs and unquantified debt exposure.

findings.subject: Sector specificity and missing exposures
findings.finding: The reviewed outputs use consumer-products demand and cost channels and introduce no insurance underwriting, reserve or investment-portfolio assumptions. Missing debt, cash, working-capital, ownership and project details remain limitations rather than invented observations.
